messages:
kate_infra: Need to provision a new GPU node pool in us-east5 for realtime-embed. Target p99 <= 100ms for 512 tokens. Cost goal < $0.08/token. Quota shows only 8 GPUs available.

josh_ops: Is p99 strict? or can we trade a few ms for cheaper SKUs?

kate_infra: p99 is strict. Plan I had: preemptible burst with A10G compact nodes + small dedicated headroom. Quota blocks full preemptible pool.

priya_sre: Heads up: adding more small GPU pools increases CA churn. We'll need CA flags tuned and distinct taints.

ton y_cloud: Two paths: 1) quota bump (48-72h) or 2) hybrid using available 8 GPUs + dedicated smaller instances. Cross-region fallback hurts p99.

alyssa_eng: What about mixed-instance-types in the same node pool? GKE doesn't allow mixed accelerators in one pool; we'd need two pools.

sara_platform: Suggest starting with 8 preemptible a10g + 3 dedicated a10g (n2-machine) as emergency fallbacks in the same region. Use taints: gpu=preemptible:NoSchedule and gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule.

ben_cost: From cost modeling, keeping mostly preemptible nets ~35% savings. But having 3 dedicated keeps p99 during preempt storms; good trade.

kate_infra: Autoscaler flags suggestions?

priya_sre: Recommended CA flags:
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
--scale-down-unneeded-time=30m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=20m
And for GPU groups increase unneeded-time to 45m during preempt cycles.

josh_ops: Also add node-group priority so dedicated node-groups have higher preservation weight.

tony_cloud: Nodepool create snippets (adjust skus):

```
gcloud container node-pools create realtime-gpu-burst \n  --cluster=prod-ai-us-east5 \n  --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g \n  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a10g,count=1 \n  --num-nodes=8 \n  --preemptible \n  --node-taints=gpu=preemptible:NoSchedule \n  --labels=pool=realtime-burst,workload=embed
```

```
gcloud container node-pools create realtime-gpu-dedicated \n  --cluster=prod-ai-us-east5 \n  --machine-type=n2-standard-16 \n  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a10g,count=1 \n  --num-nodes=3 \n  --node-taints=gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule \n  --labels=pool=realtime-dedicated,workload=embed
```

alyssa_eng: If node autoprovisioning is on, restrict to GPU families to avoid tiny cpu-only nodes being created:

```
resourceLimits:
- resourceType: "nvidia.com/gpu"
  minimum: 1
  maximum: 24
allowedMachineTypes:
- a2-*
- n2-*
```

priya_sre: Runbook for preemption storms (short):
1) Alert when preempt_rate > 20% for 10m or FailedScaleUpEvents spike.
2) Increase CA scale-down-unneeded-time to 60m.
3) Signal realtime service to reduce batch size to 256 for 5m.
4) If preempt_rate > 40% for 10m, failover routing to dedicated nodes and page oncall.
5) Rewarm KV cache and verify embed model cache hit-rate.

kate_infra: I'll open quota ticket and queue pool creation as soon as we have confirmation. dev-bot can you create a ticket?

dev-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-9781 "us-east5 gpu quota bump + hybrid pool for realtime-embed" assigned to @tony_cloud.

ton y_cloud: Taking INFRA-9781. I'll also add CA weights and alert rules to the prod-cluster terraform.

ben_cost: Add a scheduled cost report for the new pools after 48h traffic test. We need token-level cost breakdown.

kate_infra: Plan: provision hybrid pools in us-east5 (8 preemptible + 3 dedicated), deploy small loadtest for p99, and keep quota bump pending. If quota delayed, we spin emergency dedicated in us-east1 and set router circuit-breaker to avoid cross-region for realtime.

priya_sre: Also add alerts: PendingDueToQuota for GPU pods, FailedScaleUpEvents, and CA flapping metric. Tag alerts to the infra runbook.

kate_infra: Thanks! I'll post a short summary in #eng-infra when pools are live. :rocket: 

sara_platform: I'll follow up on Terraform changes and nodepool naming conventions. Keep names short and consistent.

kate_infra: awesome, thanks everyone.
